sources.citation: Philip JH. Gas Man(R) Workbook and Laboratory Manual. Chestnut Hill, MA: Med Man Simulations, Inc.; document dated 2012-05-16, preface dated October 2010. Appendix B, 'The Gas Man Approach', Model Parameters table (Table A-1), page 168.
sources.note: Tier 3, reference implementation, CITED AND NOT ADOPTED - the only entry in any of this project's data files where the Workbook is cited and the value taken from it is not the value stored (see docs/MODEL.md, 'Source hierarchy'). READ AT THE SOURCE 2026-09-06, from a copy of the front matter and appendices supplied by the project owner; this repository does not hold it, because it is publisher-copyright material and the repository is public. Page 168's Model Parameters table gives, under Volume / Flow / Rel. Flow: Circuit 8.0; Alveoli 2.5; Blood 5.00; VRG 6.0, 3.80, 0.76; Muscle 33.0, 0.90, 0.18; Fat 14.5, 0.30, 0.06. SO THE PUBLISHED CIRCUIT VOLUME IS 8.0 L AND THIS FILE STORES 6.0 L. That is a deliberate departure and not a transcription error: the project owner ruled on 2026-09-01 that which value is used is not critical here, and 6.0 was already the shipped figure. It is recorded so that a later reader finds a decision rather than an accident, which is the whole reason this file exists (PL-4YY1). WHAT THE DEPARTURE IS WORTH, SINCE THE READER SHOULD NOT HAVE TO WORK IT OUT. The circuit's fresh-gas wash-in time constant is tau_C = V_C / VdotF, so at this file's 4.0 L/min it is 90 s here against 120 s at the published 8.0 L - a 25 percent shorter machine lag. That lag is the part of the early rise in inspired concentration that belongs to the apparatus rather than to uptake, which is the single most-taught point about a circle system, so the difference is visible on the curve even though it changes nothing about the patient. A run reproducing a published Gas Man trajectory must set 8.0 L rather than assume it. THE TABLE SUPPLIES NO FRESH GAS FLOW AT ALL. Its Circuit row carries a volume and no entry in the Flow column, and the interface defaults described at page 183 ('Patient default options include:', Appendix E) are qualitative and carry no numbers. So default_fresh_gas_flow_l_min has no counterpart in this source and none in any other this project has reached; the provenance_gap below says so rather than leaving the silence to be read as an oversight.

sources.citation: De Wolf AM, Van Zundert TC, De Cooman S, Hendrickx JF. Theoretical effect of hyperventilation on speed of recovery and risk of rehypnotization following recovery - a Gas Man simulation. BMC Anesthesiology. 2012;12:22. DOI 10.1186/1471-2253-12-22. Methods.
sources.note: Tier 3, reference implementation, cited and not adopted. READ AT FULL TEXT 2026-09-13 from PubMed Central (PMC3502091). Its Methods state the settings held constant across every simulation in that study: 'a 70 kg patient, an anesthesia breathing circuit volume of 8 L, a FGF of 1 L.min-1, an alveolar minute ventilation (VA) of 5 L.min-1, a functional residual capacity (FRC) of 2.5 L, and a cardiac output (Q) of 5 L.min-1'. IT IS HERE AS THE REACHABLE CONFIRMATION OF THE 8 L FIGURE, AND FOR NOTHING ELSE. The Workbook entry above is the primary statement of Gas Man's circuit volume and it cannot be opened from a URL; this paper prints the same 8 L and is open access, so a reader can check that this file's departure is from 8 and not from something else. Two tier-3 documents agreeing is not evidence that either descends from a measurement. ITS FGF OF 1 L/min IS NOT A GAS MAN DEFAULT AND IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT THE VALUE STORED HERE. It is the operating point that study chose, stated as such, alongside an alveolar ventilation of 5 L/min that this project also does not use (the reference patient stores 4.0). Reading a study's chosen settings as a parameter set's defaults is the error this note exists to forestall.

provenance_gap: NO SOURCE IS ADOPTED FOR EITHER VALUE IN THIS FILE, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF WRITING IT DOWN. Both were hardcoded as dataclass field defaults in src/anesthesia_sim/core/circuit.py until 2026-09-13, where tools/doc_check.py's check_provenance could not see them: that check walks data files in both directions, so a scientific constant that never entered one was structurally invisible to the only tool built to catch a missing citation. PL-4YY1 moved them here for that reason, and changed neither. circuit_volume_l = 6.0 departs deliberately from the Workbook's published 8.0, on the project owner's ruling of 2026-09-01 that which value is used is not critical; the Workbook entry above carries the figure, the decision and what the 25 percent shorter machine lag looks like on the curve. default_fresh_gas_flow_l_min = 4.0 has no published counterpart at all. The Workbook's parameter table gives the circuit no flow entry, its interface defaults are described without numbers, and the two Gas Man simulation studies this project has read chose their own flows for their own purposes (De Wolf et al. 1 L/min; Meybohm et al. 10 L/min for washout). It is a project convention, chosen as a routine mid-range clinical fresh gas flow that sits well inside the supported interval core/supported_ranges.py declares (0.0 to 10.0 L/min) and puts the circuit time constant at 90 s - long enough that a learner sees the machine lag as a distinct phase of the early rise, short enough that it resolves inside the first few minutes of a teaching run. That is a design rationale and not a measurement, and it is labelled as one here. WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS GAP is a published circle-system internal volume measured on real apparatus, and a stated clinical convention for a default flow; neither has been sought yet, and neither is required for a value the owner has ruled non-critical.
